slides.title: Budgeting on a single income
slides.sub: No second paycheck to absorb the surprises. Here's how to build a budget that holds anyway.

slides.title: Start with 50 / 30 / 20
slides.note: First, track what you really spend. Most people underestimate food and subscriptions.

slides.title: Build the cushion first
slides.body: Three to six months of essentials is the goal. If that feels far off, start with $500 to $1,000 so one bad week doesn't land on a credit card.

slides.title: Pay yourself first
slides.body: Set an automatic transfer to savings the day your paycheck lands. Don't wait to save whatever's left at month's end.

slides.title: Hunt the recurring costs
slides.body: Audit subscriptions every few months. Negotiate internet and insurance. Ask your utility about budget billing.

slides.title: Small habits beat big moves.
slides.body: All nine steps for a one-income household are on the blog at singles-life.app
